title: Patscherkofel Cable Car Innsbruck-Igls
name: Patscherkofel Cable Car Innsbruck-Igls
kurzbeschreibung: The Patscherkofelbahn in Innsbruck-Igls: a modern 10-passenger gondola to Innsbruck's iconic local mountain at 1,965 m featuring the Zirbenweg and Olympic heritage.
beschreibung:
Overview

The state-of-the-art Patscherkofelbahn is located in the southern Innsbruck holiday village of Igls at the foot of Innsbruck's iconic local mountain, the Patscherkofel, at a valley elevation of around 900 metres. Rebuilt in 2017 as a highly comfortable monocable gondola, the 10-passenger cabins silently transport mountain enthusiasts in two sections up to the summit station at 1,965 metres above sea level. Visibly prominent across the region with its characteristic rounded dome and distinctive broadcast mast, Innsbruck's home mountain twice hosted the Olympic Winter Games (1964 and 1976) and serves as the gateway to one of Europe's largest stone pine forests.

Zirbenweg, Alpine Garden & Panoramic Vistas

At the mountain station, a breathtaking panoramic vista opens up over the Inntal valley, the Stubai glacier world, the Karwendel, and the Tuxer Alpen. Starting directly at the mountain station is the world-renowned Zirbenweg: along an approximately seven-kilometre gently undulating high-altitude trail, hikers walk through one of the oldest and largest continuous stone pine forests in the Alps towards the Glungezer. Directly below the top station lies the Alpengarten des Botanischen Instituts der Universität Innsbruck—Austria's highest botanical showcase garden—where over 400 rare alpine plant species from across the globe flourish. For families, the interactive Kofele-Erlebnisweg features hands-on nature play stations around the mountain hubs.

Visit & Getting There

During the summer season from late May to late October, the Patscherkofelbahn operates daily from 08:30 to 17:00 (extended until 23:00 on Thursdays for the popular evening rides). Mountain lift fares (2025/2026 season): round trip adults approx. €28.50, seniors approx. €25.50, youths approx. €22.50, children approx. €14.50. Holders of the Innsbruck Card ride once free of charge! Getting there by car: Via the Brennerautobahn A13 (Innsbruck-Süd exit) to Igls; car parks are situated along Römerstraße at the valley station (free for cable car passengers). By public transport: From Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof main station, IVB bus line J runs every 10 minutes directly to the valley station of the Patscherkofelbahn.

Tips

The entire Patscherkofelbahn, all stations, and the Restaurant Das Kofel at the top station are completely barrier-free and wheelchair accessible. The expansive sun terrace of Das Kofel serves authentic Tyrolean delicacies along with an incomparable sunset view across the Nordkette range.
